concept.name: Marubozu
concept.definition: A long-bodied candlestick with no (or almost no) shadows, so that the open and close coincide with the period's extreme prices: a white/green marubozu opens at the low and closes at the high, and a black/red marubozu opens at the high and closes at the low. It is read as one-sided dominance throughout the period and is usually interpreted as a continuation signal.
concept.intuition: One side controlled the entire session from the first trade to the last: buyers never let price dip below the open (bullish marubozu) or sellers never let it rise above the open (bearish marubozu).
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: the real body spans essentially the full high-low range, with upper and lower shadows at or near zero. Partial variants exist: an opening marubozu lacks a shadow only at the open side, a closing marubozu only at the close side.
concept.failure_modes: A single marubozu late in an extended move can mark exhaustion (a climactic final push) rather than continuation. On very short timeframes or illiquid instruments, shadowless candles occur routinely and carry little information.
concept.misconceptions: It is not a guarantee the trend continues; context matters, and a marubozu into strong resistance or support often precedes a pullback rather than immediate follow-through.
concept.example: A stock opens at 25.00, its session low, and grinds upward all day to close at 26.40, its session high. This white marubozu shows uninterrupted buying pressure and is read as supporting continuation of the advance.
